summary.oneLiner: A globally recognised precision-engineering company and leader in the organised bearing cage industry, positioned as a trusted Tier-1 partner to the world's leading bearing manufacturers.
summary.business: Harsha Engineers International Limited manufactures precision-engineered bearing cages, brass castings and automotive components (stampings, journal bearings/bushings) for global bearing manufacturers and automotive OEMs, and also undertakes EPC and O&M of solar power plants. It offers a diversified portfolio of over 7,500 specialised engineering products to customers across more than 31 countries and 5 continents.

currentContext.strengths: Longstanding relationships with all six of the world's leading bearing manufacturers, positioning HEIL as a trusted Tier-1 engineering partner in the global industrial supply chain|Leadership in the organised bearing cage industry|Broad, diversified product portfolio (7,500+ specialised engineering products) reducing dependency on any single customer or market|Balanced domestic and international customer base (39.14% of turnover from exports across 31 countries) supporting business continuity|Positioned to benefit from the 'China Plus One' sourcing shift as global manufacturers seek partners with vertically integrated forging and heat-treatment capabilities
currentContext.strategies: The Notice of AGM includes an ordinary business item to declare a final dividend on equity shares for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, to be approved by shareholders at the 16th AGM (July 23, 2026); no broader dividend policy, payout ratio, buyback or debt-reduction philosophy statement is disclosed within this bundle.
currentContext.expansion: HEIL's Engineering business is expanding its manufacturing footprint through the operationalisation of the Bhayla facility (Harsha Engineers Advantek Limited, HEAL) in India and an ongoing Phase II capacity expansion in China. The first phase of the Bhayla facility was commissioned during FY26, a milestone in domestic manufacturing scale-up, and HEAL is expected to see significant improvement in capacity utilisation and revenue contribution in 2026-27, while the Company progresses a second phase of expansion at the site. The China brownfield expansion project (at Harsha Precision Bearing Components (China) Co. Ltd's Changshu plant) is expected to become operational in the second half of 2027-28, strengthening the Company's long-term manufacturing capabilities in the region. Management continues to focus on improving profitability in Romania (Harsha Engineers Europe SRL) through better product mix, higher cage contribution and cost optimisation, with turnaround execution still underway there. On the renewable-energy side, the Company commissioned a 10.4 MW ground-mounted Solar Tracker PV Power Plant at Wada, Kankrej, Banaskantha, Gujarat (comprising 2x5.20 MWp, commissioned May 23, 2025) for captive use, in addition to existing solar (1.013 MW Solar Hybrid and 0.749 MW Solar Rooftop at Changodar; 0.855 MW Solar Rooftop and 0.395 MW Tapper Solar Rooftop at Moraiya; 1 MW Solar Mounted at Tarapur) and wind (1.25 MW windmill at Kalyanpur; 2.7 MW Wind Hybrid and 1.013 MW Solar Hybrid at Pipaliya) installations. Total capex incurred by HEIL on a consolidated basis during 2025-26 was Rs.14,669 lakhs net (capital additions of Rs.28,814 lakhs less a Rs.14,145 lakhs downward adjustment from negative movement in capital work-in-progress). Total bearing cages produced by HEIL's Engineering division during 2025-26 was 7,278.07 lakhs (units as stated in the Operational Overview). Near-term margin pressure has been flagged from capacity ramp-up and fixed-cost absorption at these new facilities.
currentContext.mdna: Global bearings market projected to grow at a 6.9% CAGR (USD 120.51bn in 2024 to USD 179.34bn by 2030), supported by expanding industrial activity, automation, technological advancement, and growing adoption of EVs and renewable energy systems - directly relevant to the Company's bearing-cage business.|EV transition requires specialised insulated bearings but reduces certain engine-related applications, tempering overall bearing demand during the transition phase.|Reshoring/localisation of manufacturing in North America and Europe is supporting regional bearing demand, though steel supply constraints and skilled-labour shortages remain challenges.|Rising demand from food-processing and medical-equipment sectors is emerging as a significant bearing-market growth driver, increasing need for food-grade stainless steel and miniature precision bearings.|Raw-material (alloy/energy price) volatility continues to impact margins, making multi-sourcing and supply-chain resilience increasingly critical for bearing manufacturers.|Indian bearings market expected to grow by approximately USD 853.9 million between 2024 and 2029 (3.2% CAGR), supported by industrialisation, infrastructure development, manufacturing growth and rising automation; 'Make in India' initiatives are encouraging domestic production and reducing import dependence.|Global metal stamping market projected to grow at a 4.26% CAGR (USD 259.35bn in 2025 to USD 377.45bn by 2034), driven by automotive, EV, medical device, aerospace and consumer-electronics demand and increasing automation/CNC adoption.|Indian metal stamping market projected to grow at a 6.3% CAGR during 2026-2033 (USD 5.2bn in 2025 to USD 8.2bn by 2033), driven by rising manufacturing activity, infrastructure expansion and automotive/industrial-equipment demand, supported by Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat policy initiatives.|Global solar market expected to grow steadily at a 3.7% CAGR (USD 282.25bn in 2025 to USD 342.55bn by 2030), supported by rising net-zero commitments, energy-storage integration and wider adoption of bifacial/high-efficiency modules - relevant to the Company's solar EPC/O&M business.|Indian GDP growth estimated at 7.6% for 2025-26, anchored in domestic demand, infrastructure expansion and improving manufacturing activity; growth projected at around 6.9% for 2026-27, with continued public capital expenditure strengthening demand across metals, mobility and engineering value chains.

risks.risk: Market concentration - a significant portion of revenue is derived from a limited number of large bearing manufacturers
risks.note: The MD&A risk table puts customer concentration first: any reduction in demand, a change in sourcing strategy, or consolidation among these key customers could adversely affect revenues. Management's answer is to diversify the revenue mix into adjacent segments - precision stampings, bushings and solar EPC - and to push into emerging and non-automotive markets, so the concentration risk is also the rationale behind the whole diversification strategy.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility in brass, steel and other metals
risks.note: HEIL names brass and steel specifically and concedes that metal price swings may compress margins in a competitive and cost-sensitive global market. Mitigation is multi-supplier sourcing with flexible procurement contracts plus pass-through pricing mechanisms with customers - pass-through is contractual rather than automatic, so timing lags between input cost and price reset remain a live margin risk.

risks.risk: Sectoral transition to electric vehicles reducing demand for conventional automotive components
risks.note: The company explicitly flags that the shift from internal combustion engine vehicles to EVs may reduce demand for certain conventional automotive components - a direct threat to the bearing-cage franchise. The stated hedge is to leverage stamping capabilities to supply EV and new-age mobility applications and to keep investing in product development aligned with evolving vehicle platforms, which makes the stamping business the structural offset to the EV risk.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange fluctuation exposure as a significant exporter
risks.note: The AR describes HEIL as a significant exporter and states that currency fluctuations could impact profitability and cash flows. Management uses hedging instruments including forward contracts and maintains a geographically diversified revenue base to reduce currency concentration - hedging shifts timing but does not remove translation exposure on the overseas operations whose recovery the MD&A credits for the year's improvement in returns.

risks.risk: Execution risk in the solar EPC business - delays, cost overruns and project execution challenges
risks.note: Solar EPC is one of the diversification legs relied upon to dilute bearing-cage concentration, and the AR flags that delays, cost overruns or execution challenges in solar EPC projects could affect margins and customer relationships. Mitigation is a structured project management framework with defined controls and close coordination with customers, vendors and contractors on timely, cost-effective execution - i.e. the diversification hedge carries its own project-delivery risk.

risks.risk: Climate transition and carbon pricing - EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) exposure on emission-intensive operations
risks.note: The BRSR material-issues register identifies climate transition as a policy and legal risk, naming CBAM as a carbon pricing mechanism that may increase costs for emission-intensive operations - directly relevant to an exporter with foundry and forging operations. The same row flags technology risk: failure to adopt modern, low-emission manufacturing technologies may limit competitiveness. The Air Pollution Compliance row adds that non-compliance with statutory emission limits could cause operational disruption including potential plant shutdown in the worst case.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity pressuring pricing, margins and market share across segments
risks.note: The MD&A states increased competition may exert pressure on pricing, margins and market share across business segments. The defence is design capability, quality, cost competitiveness and timely delivery, plus stronger customer relationships and expanded value-added offerings - which is a reminder that the moat rests on engineering/design capability rather than on price.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and supplier dependence affecting production schedules
risks.note: The company flags that supply chain disruptions, logistics constraints or supplier-related issues may impact production schedules and customer commitments - material when a limited set of large bearing customers depend on committed delivery. Mitigation is alternate sourcing options, supplier diversification, continuous supply chain monitoring and proactive engagement with critical vendors.

one-line thesis: Harsha Engineers delivered robust FY26 growth (Engg. rev +14%, EBITDA ~INR270cr adj) driven by export recovery and bushing demand, while absorbing startup losses from Advantek and Romania; the thesis hinges on Advantek's 3x revenue ramp in FY27 and China expansion completing in H2FY28 to unlock consolidated margin expansion.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Engg INR1,444cr (+14% YoY), Solar INR183cr; EBITDA: Engg INR264cr reported (INR270cr adj, +19% YoY adj), Margin ~18.7% reported (~18.3% prior yr adj); PAT: Solar INR10.2cr (vs INR5cr adj prior), Subsidiaries combined loss INR21.6cr (Advantek -INR11.4cr, Romania -INR14cr, China +INR5cr); Order Book: Not disclosed (make-to-order); Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, Capex INR120cr funded; One-offs: Labor code impact (INR6cr), Advantek depreciation/interest drag, Romania wind sector weakness.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Double-digit consolidated, India Engg mid-to-high teens (15-19%); Margin: Maintain current profile, target 100-200bps expansion over 2-3 years; Order Inflow: Strong in bushings/large cages; Capex: INR30-40cr maintenance (India), INR70cr (China FY27), INR20cr (China FY28), Phase-2 Advantek planning underway.
order book & pipeline: Make-to-order model; visibility driven by SKU pipeline (8,000+ SKUs, 500-600 new/year); Bushing order book strong due to wind gearbox design conversion; Large cage wallet share gains pending execution.
segment / subsidiary detail: Cages: Large-size +14% to INR49cr, Japan customer +12% to INR73cr; Bushings: INR127cr (+25% YoY), targeting 25-30% growth FY27; Stampings: INR60cr, targeting >20% growth; Solar: INR183cr rev, INR10.2cr PAT; Geography: Europe 30%, China >10%, US 6-7%, Japan 2%.
growth verticals / optionality: Advantek ramp-up (target INR250-300cr rev at peak current capacity, 3x sales growth FY27); China brownfield expansion (steel cages mix shift, operational H2FY28); Wallet share gains in Europe/US (consolidation of competitors, current 10-20% share vs potential); Bushing design conversion in wind sector.
margins & cost dynamics: Consolidated EBITDA margin pressure from Romania (-ve EBITDA) and Advantek (depreciation/interest); India Engg margin stable at ~22%; Raw material (brass/steel) pass-through mechanism active (4-month lag); Labor code headwind INR6cr normalized in adj EBITDA.
capex / expansion: FY26 Total: INR120cr; FY27 Plan: INR30-40cr (India maintenance) + INR70cr (China expansion) + Phase-2 Advantek (quantum TBD, starts FY27); FY28 Plan: INR20cr (China completion).
capital allocation: Priority on capacity expansion (China, Advantek Phase-2) and working capital (cycle ~130 days); Subsidiary losses being absorbed via internal accruals/debt; No dividend guidance specific in transcript, focus on reinvestment for growth.
risks & watch-items: Romania turnaround delay (wind sector stagnation, negative EBITDA); Advantek utilization ramp slower than expected; Global macro turmoil impacting Europe/US auto demand; Raw material volatility despite pass-through; Execution risk on China brownfield project.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; confident on India/Export growth trajectory; transparent on subsidiary losses (Romania/Advantek) but firm on turnaround plans; defensive on margin guidance (maintain vs expand immediately).
non-obvious takeaways: Romania's underperformance is specifically tied to wind gearbox demand stagnation despite global renewable tailwinds; US tariff removal on cages is an immediate catalyst for export volume; Management explicitly states they are NOT diversifying beyond cages/stampings/bushings into other bearing components (rings) to focus on wallet share depth.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wind turbine manufacturers need reliable bushing supply amid design conversion from traditional to planetary gearboxes; Harsha is capturing this specific technical shift. | Harsha Engineers Int Ltd | beneficiary | High | Bushing segment growing 25-30% with clear technical moat in wind gearbox conversion; INR127cr base expanding rapidly. |
| European bearing majors face consolidation and cost pressure, seeking outsourcing partners with multi-material competency (steel/brass/polyamide) outside high-cost zones. | Harsha Engineers Int Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Wallet share currently only 10-20% with major EU customers; consolidation of local competitors opens door for Harsha's India/China capacity. |
| US import tariffs previously hindered cage exports; recent reduction to zero removes cost disadvantage for Indian exporters. | Harsha Engineers Int Ltd | beneficiary | High | Management cited US export pickup directly linked to tariff removal; US segment ~6-7% of rev has high elasticity. |
| Romania subsidiary struggling with negative EBITDA due to wind sector weakness and high fixed costs; turnaround uncertain in near term. | Harsha Engineers Int Ltd (Romania Unit) | loser | Med | INR14cr loss in FY26; management admits 'hazy picture' on Europe demand sustainability; drag on consolidated margins until mix shifts to cages (30%+ target). |
